nodes.description: Opacity in the pupillary region in the two relatives carrying the exon 2 deletion.

evidence.reference_title: Novel crystallin gamma B mutations in a Kuwaiti family with autosomal dominant congenital cataracts reveal genetic and clinical heterogeneity.
evidence.snippet: The heterozygous g.167delC, Exon 2 mutation (numbered starting from the first ATG codon) was detected in two of the affected family members (I-1 and III-2) who had anterior polar cataracts.

meta.association: Reported causative; evidence limited to one family

evidence.reference_title: Novel crystallin gamma B mutations in a Kuwaiti family with autosomal dominant congenital cataracts reveal genetic and clinical heterogeneity.
evidence.snippet: This study is the first to report a mutation in the human CRYGB gene.

evidence.reference_title: Novel crystallin gamma B mutations in a Kuwaiti family with autosomal dominant congenital cataracts reveal genetic and clinical heterogeneity.
evidence.snippet: Neither of these mutations was detected in 50 healthy subjects, including the unaffected family members.

evidence.reference_title: Evaluating gene-disease relationship strength in crystallin genes in association with pediatric cataracts.
evidence.snippet: Two genes (CRYGA, CRYGS) as Moderate; and four genes have Limited support (CRYBA2, CRYBA4, CRYBB3 and CRYGB).

evidence.reference_title: Candidate Genes for Non-Syndromic Pediatric Cataracts.
evidence.snippet: While two studies report a possible association of heterozygous CRYGB variants with pediatric cataracts, their causal relationship remains inconclusive

nodes.description: Reported human alleles are a heterozygous single-base deletion in exon 2 (g.167delC) that shifts the reading frame and truncates the protein, and a heterozygous single-base deletion in intron 1 (g.67delG) whose effect on splicing was not tested. Mouse alleles that cause dominant cataract are a truncation of the fourth Greek key motif (Crygb nop) and the missense changes I4F and S11R.

evidence.reference_title: Novel crystallin gamma B mutations in a Kuwaiti family with autosomal dominant congenital cataracts reveal genetic and clinical heterogeneity.
evidence.snippet: These mutations included a heterozygous g.67delG, intron 1 deletion in four of the affected family members with lamellar cataracts and a heterozygous g.167delC, exon 2 deletion inherited from the Egyptian grandmother by her granddaughter, resulting in anterior polar cataracts.

evidence.reference_title: Novel crystallin gamma B mutations in a Kuwaiti family with autosomal dominant congenital cataracts reveal genetic and clinical heterogeneity.
evidence.snippet: The mutant protein is expected to contain the first 24 amino acids of the wild-type protein, and the subsequent deletion results in a frame shift, generating 19 nonconserved amino acids before translation termination

evidence.reference_title: Three murine cataract mutants (Cat2) are defective in different gamma-crystallin genes.
evidence.snippet: The mutant allele Crygbnop (formerly Cat2(nop)) is caused by a replacement of 11 bp by 4 bp in the third exon of Crygb

nodes.description: Crystallin degradation products increase in S11R lenses in step with the nuclear cataract and are attributed to calcium-dependent proteolysis.

evidence.reference_title: Dense nuclear cataract caused by the gammaB-crystallin S11R point mutation.
evidence.snippet: Western blotting showed an increased degradation of crystallin proteins correlated with the nuclear cataract.

nodes.description: Removal of the opacified lens is the management of visually significant congenital cataract; nearly all affected members of the reported family had surgery early in life. No CRYGB-specific therapy exists.

evidence.reference_title: Novel crystallin gamma B mutations in a Kuwaiti family with autosomal dominant congenital cataracts reveal genetic and clinical heterogeneity.
evidence.snippet: However, these studies could not be performed in this family because all of the affected family members (except I-1) underwent surgery at an early age, and their lens tissues were not preserved.

nodes.id: Crygb S11R mouse with Gja8 Cx46 knock-in

nodes.description: The S10R (S11R in the numbering that counts the initiator methionine) mouse protein keeps an essentially native structure, but some of its cysteines become reactive and form intermolecular disulfide crosslinks, so the protein aggregates without unfolding.
nodes.id: Cysteine Oxidation and Disulfide Crosslinking of Gamma-B Crystallin

evidence.reference_title: Oxidation of active cysteines mediates protein aggregation of S10R, the cataract-associated mutant of mouse GammaB-crystallin.
evidence.snippet: This occurs even as the protein structure is essentially unaltered. Thus, the primary event is enhanced protein aggregation due to the disulfide crosslinking of the mutant protein.

nodes.description: Congenital cataract in all affected members of the reported family. The member who inherited both CRYGB variants had complete cataract. It is bound to the general congenital cataract term because an OLS4 search of HPO for "total cataract" returned no terms and "complete cataract" returned no cataract term.

evidence.reference_title: Novel crystallin gamma B mutations in a Kuwaiti family with autosomal dominant congenital cataracts reveal genetic and clinical heterogeneity.
evidence.snippet: Another patient with complete cataracts was a compound heterozygote with both of the above-mentioned mutations.

evidence.reference_title: Novel crystallin gamma B mutations in a Kuwaiti family with autosomal dominant congenital cataracts reveal genetic and clinical heterogeneity.
evidence.snippet: This study is the first to report complex heterogeneous mutations in the CRYGB gene resulting in ADCC with three distinct phenotypes (lamellar, anterior polar, and complete cataracts) in the same family.

nodes.description: From embryonic day 15.5 Crygb nop fiber cells swell, and by birth the primary fiber cells at the lens centre are disorganized and the centre remains opaque.
nodes.id: Disorganization of Primary Lens Fiber Cells

evidence.reference_title: Altered aggregation properties of mutant gamma-crystallins cause inherited cataract.
evidence.snippet: This process continues in the newborn mouse where, in contrast to the wild-type lens (E), the centre of the Crygbnop lens remains opaque and the primary lens fibre cells become completely disorganized

nodes.description: Mutant I4F gamma-B crystallin, unlike wild type, binds alpha-crystallin and forms high-molecular-weight complexes in the lens and in vitro.
nodes.id: Gamma-B Crystallin Binding to Alpha-Crystallin in High-Molecular-Weight Complexes

evidence.reference_title: Crystallin {gamma}B-I4F mutant protein binds to {alpha}-crystallin and affects lens transparency.
evidence.snippet: Unlike wild type gammaB, the gammaB-I4F mutant protein binds to alpha-crystallin to form high molecular weight complexes in vivo and in vitro.

nodes.description: Truncating and some missense mouse Crygb alleles produce a protein that is unlikely to adopt its native fold or is less stable than wild type. Mutant nop gamma-B crystallin readily forms amyloid fibrils in vitro, unlike the wild-type protein. Whether the human exon 2 truncation behaves this way has not been tested.

evidence.reference_title: Altered aggregation properties of mutant gamma-crystallins cause inherited cataract.
evidence.snippet: In vitro, recombinant mutant gammaB-crystallin readily formed amyloid fibrils under physiological buffer conditions, unlike wild-type protein.

evidence.reference_title: Crystallin {gamma}B-I4F mutant protein binds to {alpha}-crystallin and affects lens transparency.
evidence.snippet: Circular dichroism measurements indicate that gammaB-I4F protein is less stable than wild type gammaB at high temperature.

nodes.description: Inner mature fiber cells of homozygous S11R lenses are disrupted and degenerate, while the peripheral layers stay normal.

evidence.reference_title: Dense nuclear cataract caused by the gammaB-crystallin S11R point mutation.
evidence.snippet: Homozygous mutant mice developed dense nuclear cataracts associated with disrupted inner lens fiber cells.

nodes.description: In Crygb nop lenses the mutant protein forms large Congo red-staining, filamentous inclusions in the nuclei of primary fiber cells. The inclusions appear before the first morphological change and before cataract.
nodes.id: Intranuclear Gamma-B Crystallin Inclusions in Primary Fiber Cells

animal_models.description: Mutant protein forms amyloid-like intranuclear inclusions in primary fiber cells before cataract appears.
animal_models.genotype: Crygb nop (11-bp to 4-bp replacement in exon 3, truncating the fourth Greek key motif)
animal_models.name: Crygb nop mouse

evidence.reference_title: Altered aggregation properties of mutant gamma-crystallins cause inherited cataract.
evidence.snippet: Their formation preceded not only the first gross morphological changes in the lens, but also the first signs of cataract. The inclusions contained filamentous material that could be stained with the amyloid-detecting dye, Congo red.

evidence.reference_title: Altered aggregation properties of mutant gamma-crystallins cause inherited cataract.
evidence.snippet: Using antibodies specific to either γEelo-crystallin (Figure 2C, arrow) or γBnop-crystallin (Figure 2D, arrow), it is clear that the intranuclear inclusions contain the detectable altered γ-crystallin proteins.

nodes.description: Lamellar cataract in the relatives carrying the intron 1 deletion.

evidence.reference_title: Novel crystallin gamma B mutations in a Kuwaiti family with autosomal dominant congenital cataracts reveal genetic and clinical heterogeneity.
evidence.snippet: Clinical and morphological results confirmed the presence of lamellar cataracts with complete penetrance in all of the patients with the g.67delG, Intron 1 mutation.

nodes.description: In homozygous Clapper (I4F) lenses the cataractous region contains darkly staining protein aggregates, enlarged spaces between fibers, and smaller, disorganized inner mature fibers.
nodes.id: Lens Fiber Protein Aggregates and Enlarged Interfiber Spaces

animal_models.description: Dominant lamellar cataract with protein aggregates and enlarged interfiber spaces.
animal_models.genotype: ENU-induced Crygb missense allele replacing isoleucine 4 with phenylalanine (I4F), heterozygous and homozygous
animal_models.name: Clapper (Crygb I4F) mouse

evidence.reference_title: Crystallin {gamma}B-I4F mutant protein binds to {alpha}-crystallin and affects lens transparency.
evidence.snippet: Darkly stained aggregates, enlarged interfiber spaces, and disorganized and smaller inner mature fibers were found in the regions of the cataract in homozygous Clapper mutant lenses.

nodes.description: Aggregated protein and damaged fiber cells scatter light, producing lens opacity. In the human family the opacity was lamellar, anterior polar or complete depending on genotype; in mice it is lamellar (I4F) or dense nuclear (S11R, nop).
nodes.id: Lens Light Scattering and Loss of Transparency

animal_models.description: Homozygous Cx46 knock-in fully prevents the S11R nuclear cataract.
animal_models.genotype: CrygbS11R/S11R; Gja8 tm1(Gja3)Tww knock-in (alpha3 connexin expressed from the alpha8 locus)
animal_models.name: Crygb S11R mouse with Gja8 Cx46 knock-in

evidence.reference_title: Crystallin {gamma}B-I4F mutant protein binds to {alpha}-crystallin and affects lens transparency.
evidence.snippet: A new mouse mutant line, Clapper, identified from N-ethyl-N-nitrosurea (ENU)-mutagenized mice, develops a dominant lamellar cataract.

evidence.reference_title: Dense nuclear cataract caused by the gammaB-crystallin S11R point mutation.
evidence.snippet: A point mutation (A to C) of the gammaB-crystallin gene, which results in the gammaB-S11R mutant protein, was identified in this cataractous mouse line.

nodes.description: F-actin staining is absent from fiber cells of the S11R lens core, where the gamma-crystallin aggregates sit.
nodes.id: Loss of F-Actin in Inner Fiber Cells

evidence.reference_title: Connexin mediated cataract prevention in mice.
evidence.snippet: F-actin staining was absent in fiber cells from the γB(S11R/S11R) lens core, but F-actin signals appeared normal in γB(S11R/S11R) α8(Kiα3/Kiα3) lenses at the same age.

nodes.description: In Crygb S11R lenses gamma-crystallin aggregates collect at the cell boundaries of inner mature fiber cells, and little gamma-crystallin remains in the cytosol.
nodes.id: Membrane-Associated Gamma-Crystallin Aggregates in Inner Fiber Cells

animal_models.description: Gamma-crystallin aggregates at inner fiber boundaries, loss of F-actin, raised calcium and dense nuclear cataract.
animal_models.genotype: Crygb p.S11R point mutation, heterozygous and homozygous
animal_models.name: Crygb S11R mouse

evidence.reference_title: Dense nuclear cataract caused by the gammaB-crystallin S11R point mutation.
evidence.snippet: Immunohistochemistry data revealed gamma-crystallin aggregates at the cell boundaries of inner mature fibers that lose actin filaments.

evidence.reference_title: Connexin mediated cataract prevention in mice.
evidence.snippet: Immunohistological staining results of F-actin and γ-crystallin revealed that γB(S11R/S11R) lenses had substantial membrane-associated γ-crystallin aggregates, a lack of F-actin and extremely low levels of cytosolic γ-crystallin in interior fiber cells.

nodes.description: Total calcium is substantially raised in S11R mutant lenses, measured by inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectrometry.

animal_models.description: Homozygous knock-in of alpha3 connexin (Cx46) prevents the nuclear cataract of S11R mice and keeps lens calcium, F-actin and crystallins normal.
animal_models.genotype: CrygbS11R/S11R; Gja8 tm1(Gja3)Tww knock-in (alpha3 connexin expressed from the alpha8 locus)
animal_models.name: Crygb S11R mouse with Gja8 Cx46 knock-in

evidence.reference_title: Dense nuclear cataract caused by the gammaB-crystallin S11R point mutation.
evidence.snippet: ICP-OES confirmed a substantial elevation of calcium concentration in mutant lenses.
